# rcnv_window_associations_v

Sliding-window rare-CNV association statistics from Collins et al. 2022, "A cross-disorder
dosage sensitivity map of the human genome" (Cell 185:3041-3055, doi
10.1016/j.cell.2022.06.036, CC-BY 4.0). One row per (phenotype, cnv_type, window) over
259,795 genomic windows: 108 (phenotype, cnv_type) groups, 17,114-257,726 rows each,
11,198,315 rows total, from the same meta-analysis of rare CNVs in 950,278 individuals as
rcnv_gene_associations_v. This is the position-keyed half of that pair: use it for "is there
a rare-CNV association anywhere in this interval", including intergenic intervals and
regions whose signal is not attributable to one gene. A WINDOW ROW IS NOT A GENE ROW. The
association is for the CNVs OVERLAPPING the window, not for any gene inside it — a 200 kb
window typically contains several genes and the signal cannot be assigned to one of them.
For a gene-level answer use rcnv_gene_associations_v, which is keyed on ensembl_gene_id and
carries the pHaplo / pTriplo scores; this view carries no gene column and no dosage-
sensitivity scores. To go from a window to the genes in it, join gene_annotations_v on
GRCh38 coordinates. COORDINATES ARE GRCh38, WITH THE GRCh37 ORIGINALS KEPT. The published
windows are a regular grid in GRCh37 — 200 kb wide, 10 kb step — and window_start_grch37 /
window_end_grch37 are those published values, traceable to the Zenodo file: this is the
window's published identity. window_start / window_end are the GRCh38 result of lifting them
(UCSC liftOver, whole interval, same chromosome, lifted length 180-220 kb) and are what to
query with, since every other view here is GRCh38 — but they are a derived coordinate, not
the window's identity. The LIFTED set is NOT a regular grid. Lifted widths run
190,000-219,265, only ~90% are exactly 200 kb, and some adjacent pairs come back in a
different order than they went in. So do not assume a 200 kb width or a 10 kb step of the
GRCh38 columns, and do not compute a window index from them. Count distinct windows on (chr,
window_start_grch37, window_end_grch37): the lift is bijective here (both pairs distinct-
count to the same 259,795), so this is not needed to get a correct count, but it is the
window's published identity and the GRCh38 pair is derived from it. Rows still overlap
heavily by construction: a single strong locus produces ~20 consecutive windows with near-
identical statistics, so "how many significant windows" is not a count of independent
signals. ONLY WINDOWS THAT LIFTED ARE HERE. 4,880 of the 267,237 published windows (1.83%)
do not lift and are absent, and the loss is not uniform: chr9 7.7% (pericentromeric), chr21
4.4%, chr22 3.6%, chr1 3.2%. A further 2,562 lifted windows have NA statistics in every
phenotype x CNV group and so reach no row here, leaving 259,795 distinct windows. Near those
regions, "no window covers this position" means the window was dropped, not that the
interval was tested and null. NO "TESTED, NO ESTIMATE" ROWS — THE OPPOSITE OF THE GENE
TABLE. rcnv_gene_associations_v keeps the 65% of gene rows whose statistics are NULL; here
those rows are dropped at munge instead, because a window with no estimate is not a fact
about any entity a caller can ask about. Every row carries a beta, a z, an mlog10p and an
mlog10_fdr_q, so `beta IS NOT NULL` is unnecessary on this view (the *_secondary columns are
still NULL for 58% of rows). The number of windows present therefore varies by phenotype and
CNV class, from 17,114 to 257,726 rows per group. SIGNIFICANCE HAS TWO TIERS, EACH GATED BY
SECONDARY EVIDENCE — the same gate as rcnv_gene_associations_v, but the primary threshold
differs: this is the paper's sliding-window rule, not its gene-based exome-wide rule. A
window is FDR significant if `mlog10_fdr_q > -LOG10(0.01)` (FDR < 1%), or genome-wide
significant if `mlog10p > -LOG10(3.74e-6)` (P <= 3.74e-6, the paper's Bonferroni threshold
for the ~13,340 non-overlapping 200 kb windows it estimates were effectively tested); either
tier additionally requires `n_nominal_cohorts >= 2` OR `mlog10p_secondary > -LOG10(0.05)`.
Thresholding on `mlog10p` or `mlog10_fdr_q` alone is not what the paper reports. PHENOTYPES
ARE HPO GROUPS, WITH TWO SPECIAL CODES, exactly as in rcnv_gene_associations_v. `phenotype`
is an HPO term id with the colon removed (HP0012759 = HP:0012759). HP0000118 ("Phenotypic
abnormality") is every case pooled (458,326 cases + 491,952 controls), so it overlaps all
the others and must not be summed with them; UNKNOWN is the group of cases matching none of
the listed terms. Join phenotypes_v on `p.dataset = w.dataset AND p.trait_original =
w.phenotype` for the name. QUERY WITH A `chr` PREDICATE. The table is partitioned by
chromosome and clustered by (phenotype, cnv_type, window_start); it is the largest table of
the rCNV product by two orders of magnitude, so a positional question should name `chr` as a
literal, and a phenotype-wide question should name `phenotype` and `cnv_type`. EFFECT SIZES
ARE ON THE LOG SCALE: `beta` is ln(odds ratio), so OR = EXP(beta).

## Columns

| column | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dataset` | `STRING` | Source dataset, constant 'Collins_rCNV_2022' |
| `phenotype` | `STRING` | HPO phenotype group code without the colon (e.g. HP0012759). HP0000118 is all cases pooled; UNKNOWN is cases matching none of the listed terms. Join phenotypes_v.trait_original for the name |
| `cnv_type` | `STRING` | CNV class tested: DEL (deletion) or DUP (duplication) |
| `chr` | `INT64` | Chromosome as an integer. Autosomes only (1-22) — the study tested no sex chromosome. The partitioning column: name it as a literal in any positional query |
| `window_start` | `INT64` | Window start in GRCh38, lifted from window_start_grch37. Query with this, not the GRCh37 pair. Lifted windows are NOT a regular grid — do not assume a 200 kb width or a 10 kb step |
| `window_end` | `INT64` | Window end in GRCh38, lifted from window_end_grch37 |
| `window_start_grch37` | `INT64` | Published GRCh37 window start. With window_end_grch37 and chr this is the window's published identity, traceable to the Zenodo file — the GRCh38 pair is derived from it, not an independent identity |
| `window_end_grch37` | `INT64` | Published GRCh37 window end. The published grid is exactly 200 kb wide with a 10 kb step; the GRCh38 pair is neither |
| `n_nominal_cohorts` | `INT64` | Number of contributing cohorts with nominal (P<0.05) evidence. One of the two ways to satisfy the paper's secondary-evidence requirement (n_nominal_cohorts >= 2, OR mlog10p_secondary > -LOG10(0.05)) alongside the primary FDR or genome-wide threshold |
| `top_cohort` | `STRING` | Cohort contributing the strongest single-cohort signal; the one dropped in the *_secondary re-analysis |
| `cohorts_excluded` | `STRING` | Semicolon-separated cohorts excluded from this meta-analysis (too few cases for this phenotype, or no CNV data). NULL where none were excluded |
| `case_freq` | `FLOAT64` | Frequency of carriers of a qualifying CNV overlapping the window among cases |
| `control_freq` | `FLOAT64` | Frequency of carriers of a qualifying CNV overlapping the window among controls |
| `beta` | `FLOAT64` | Effect size as ln(odds ratio) — OR = EXP(beta). Never NULL on this view: rows without an estimate are dropped at munge, unlike rcnv_gene_associations_v |
| `beta_lower` | `FLOAT64` | Lower bound of the 95% CI on beta, ln scale |
| `beta_upper` | `FLOAT64` | Upper bound of the 95% CI on beta, ln scale |
| `z` | `FLOAT64` | Meta-analysis Z score |
| `mlog10p` | `FLOAT64` | -log10 of the meta-analysis p-value. Genome-wide significance in the paper is P <= 3.74e-6 (the Bonferroni threshold for ~13,340 non-overlapping windows), i.e. mlog10p > -LOG10(3.74e-6), plus the secondary-evidence requirement — see the view description |
| `mlog10_fdr_q` | `FLOAT64` | -log10 of the FDR q-value. The paper's FDR-significance threshold is FDR < 1%, i.e. mlog10_fdr_q > -LOG10(0.01), plus the same secondary-evidence requirement |
| `beta_secondary` | `FLOAT64` | beta from the leave-top-cohort-out re-analysis. NULL for 58% of rows |
| `beta_lower_secondary` | `FLOAT64` | Lower 95% CI bound of beta_secondary, ln scale |
| `beta_upper_secondary` | `FLOAT64` | Upper 95% CI bound of beta_secondary, ln scale |
| `z_secondary` | `FLOAT64` | Z score from the leave-top-cohort-out re-analysis |
| `mlog10p_secondary` | `FLOAT64` | -log10 p-value from the leave-top-cohort-out re-analysis |
| `mlog10_fdr_q_secondary` | `FLOAT64` | -log10 FDR q-value from the leave-top-cohort-out re-analysis |
| `resource` | `STRING` | Data source identifier, constant 'rcnv' — the same resource dosage_sensitivity_v, rcnv_gene_associations_v and rcnv_segments_v carry |

Types are the view's own BigQuery types. Match the literal to the type: a quoted string
never compares equal to a numeric column, and an ARRAY column has to go through UNNEST
(`<value> IN UNNEST(<column>)`), never a bare `=`.

## Worked examples

Queries that run against rcnv_window_associations_v as written. Copy the shape rather than
inventing one — each shows the filters this view expects.

### Is there a rare-CNV signal at a fine-mapped GWAS locus? Takes the high-PIP credible-set variants of one FinnGen quantitative trait on one chromosome and reports the deletion windows covering each lead position — chosen because its lead variant sits inside 16p11.2, a well-known recurrent-CNV region, and the join lands on genome-wide-significant deletion windows there. The literal `chr = 16` appears on BOTH sides — in the CTE it prunes credible_sets_v's partitions, on the window view it prunes this table's, and the join's `cs.chr = w.chr` alone would prune neither. Windows overlap, so one position falls in ~20 of them with near-identical statistics.

```sql
WITH cs AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT chr, pos, variant, pip
  FROM credible_sets_v
  WHERE chr = 16 AND resource = 'finngen' AND data_type = 'GWAS'
    AND trait_original = 'median_3035941_age_adjusted_IRN' AND pip > 0.5
)
SELECT cs.variant, ROUND(cs.pip, 3) AS pip,
       w.window_start, w.window_end,
       w.window_start_grch37, w.window_end_grch37,
       ROUND(EXP(w.beta), 2) AS odds_ratio,
       ROUND(w.mlog10p, 2) AS mlog10p,
       ROUND(w.mlog10_fdr_q, 2) AS mlog10_fdr_q
FROM rcnv_window_associations_v w
JOIN cs ON cs.chr = w.chr AND cs.pos BETWEEN w.window_start AND w.window_end
WHERE w.chr = 16 AND w.cnv_type = 'DEL' AND w.phenotype = 'HP0012759'
ORDER BY w.mlog10p DESC
LIMIT 20
```

### Which phenotypes a deletion of one region is associated with: the single strongest window per phenotype in chr16:29-31 Mb (GRCh38, the 16p11.2 recurrent-CNV region), strongest first. The overlap test is `window_start < end AND window_end > start`, not BETWEEN — a window is wanted if it intersects the region, and BETWEEN on window_start alone would miss the windows that start before it. Reducing to one row per phenotype is what makes the result readable; without it the ~200 overlapping windows per phenotype swamp it.

```sql
SELECT w.phenotype, p.trait_name,
       w.window_start, w.window_end,
       w.window_start_grch37, w.window_end_grch37,
       w.n_nominal_cohorts,
       ROUND(EXP(w.beta), 2) AS odds_ratio,
       ROUND(w.mlog10p, 2) AS mlog10p,
       ROUND(w.mlog10_fdr_q, 2) AS mlog10_fdr_q
FROM rcnv_window_associations_v w
LEFT JOIN phenotypes_v p
  ON p.dataset = w.dataset AND p.trait_original = w.phenotype
WHERE w.chr = 16
  AND w.window_start < 31000000 AND w.window_end > 29000000
  AND w.cnv_type = 'DEL'
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY w.phenotype ORDER BY w.mlog10p DESC) = 1
ORDER BY mlog10p DESC
LIMIT 15
```

### FDR-significant deletion windows genome-wide for one HPO group, at the paper's own rule: FDR < 1% AND (nominal evidence in at least two cohorts OR the leave-top-cohort-out secondary p-value still nominally significant). This is the one shape with no `chr` literal, because the question is genome-wide; the (phenotype, cnv_type) clustering prefix is what limits the scan instead. The result is windows, not loci — consecutive rows are the same signal seen through a sliding window, so collapse adjacent windows before counting regions.

```sql
SELECT w.phenotype, p.trait_name, w.cnv_type,
       w.chr, w.window_start, w.window_end,
       w.n_nominal_cohorts,
       ROUND(EXP(w.beta), 2) AS odds_ratio,
       ROUND(w.mlog10p, 2) AS mlog10p,
       ROUND(w.mlog10_fdr_q, 2) AS mlog10_fdr_q
FROM rcnv_window_associations_v w
JOIN phenotypes_v p
  ON p.dataset = w.dataset AND p.trait_original = w.phenotype
WHERE w.phenotype = 'HP0012759' AND w.cnv_type = 'DEL'
  AND w.mlog10_fdr_q > -LOG10(0.01)
  AND (w.n_nominal_cohorts >= 2 OR w.mlog10p_secondary > -LOG10(0.05))
ORDER BY w.mlog10_fdr_q DESC
LIMIT 50
```
